text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad praised private power producers for carrying out their social obligations, especially at places where their plants are located.
-- Members of syndicates involved in cloning of mobile phone numbers for fraud will be detained uner the Internal Security Act, said deputy police chief Norian Mai.
-- Water treatment firm Puncak Niaga has been awarded a management contract to operate a facility with production capacity of 545 million litres a day in central Selangor state.

-- A plan to double-track and electrify the railway from Kualai in southern Johor state to Singapore has been scrapped as Singapore wanted a different track system, said Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik.

-- Securities Commission chairman Munir Majid said it was time to consider the setting up of a panel of experts to oversee the regulatory aspects of the capital markets due to rapid changes taking place in the industry.
